prompt.context: Your client, AllHealthy, is one of the largest health plans in the United States with over 30,000 employees. They are facing drastic changes in the health care industry. Healthcare reforms have pushed AllHealthy to pursue a route of customer-centric strategies. To remain competitive with the rise of Health Care Exchanges, your client has decided to implement a Client Relationship Management (CRM) system in order to enhance the customer and employee experience. Currently, contact center associates have no visibility into customer call history. When a customer calls with a follow-up question, new cases are created in AllHealthy's legacy CRM system instead of being attached to the original case. Additionally, when calls are transferred, the next associate does not have the previous call history and must re-ask demographic and issue questions. This process decreases customer satisfaction and leads to re-work and decreased productivity for contact center associates.
prompt.question: You are the change management lead for the new CRM system adoption project. AllHealthy wants to understand how you will help them prepare their business for this large-scale change. Address the following in your plan: (1) Who are the stakeholders and how will you communicate to them? (2) What are the change issues and how will you address them? (3) How will you measure success?

clarifying_info.q: How many contact center associates are affected?
clarifying_info.a: The company has over 30,000 employees total; contact center associates are the primary affected group but the change touches the entire organization.

clarifying_info.q: What is the timeline for the CRM rollout?
clarifying_info.a: The case does not specify a timeline; assume a standard large-scale IT adoption project.

clarifying_info.q: Is there an existing change management structure or champions network?
clarifying_info.a: Not currently in place; that is part of what you need to design.

clarifying_info.q: What is the budget or scope for training?
clarifying_info.a: Not specified; focus on the approach rather than cost.

questions.prompt: Who are the stakeholders and how will you communicate with each group?
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify at least four stakeholder groups: (1) Leadership at all levels, (2) Contact center associates (primary users), (3) Customers (indirect beneficiaries), (4) Rest of the organization (affected by process changes). Communication approach should leverage existing channels and policies, identify change champions and change agents (some as system super-users), use videos to explain why the new CRM creates value, and solicit honest feedback through anonymous surveys.

questions.prompt: What are the key change management issues and how will you address each?
questions.guidance: Candidate should structure around five issues: (1) Leadership alignment — top leadership buy-in is not enough; all leadership levels must understand the reasons for change and how they will be rewarded. (2) Employee buy-in — resistance is inevitable; change agent networks should be set up with speaking points to engage the broader organization and demonstrate leadership unity. (3) Communications — early, clear, and consistent communication plans manage negative perceptions and facilitate feedback; mistrust rises when employees are surprised. (4) Training — must be concise yet thorough, account for knowledge gaps, include competency tests, and plan for continued adoption post-deployment. (5) Incentives — tie adoption to Performance Management or establish explicit benefits to motivate use.

questions.prompt: How will you measure the success of the CRM adoption?
questions.guidance: Candidate should recommend defining a collective, measurable set of metrics at the start of the project from three perspectives: leadership, customers, and contact center associates. Example metrics include: 75% of employees trained, logged in, and actively using the new system by end of deployment; improved customer satisfaction scores on surveys related to call quality; improved employee satisfaction and productivity as measured by surveys and call metrics such as call issue resolution time and number of open issues past due.

brainstorming.prompt: What additional change management levers or risks should AllHealthy consider for this CRM implementation?

categories.name: Leadership & Governance
ideas: Executive sponsor visibly championing the project
Regular leadership alignment check-ins throughout rollout

categories.name: People & Culture
ideas: Identify and empower change champions at every level
Address fear of job displacement or performance scrutiny
Celebrate early adopters and quick wins publicly

categories.name: Communications
ideas: Multi-channel plan (email, town halls, intranet, video)
FAQ document updated in real time as questions arise

categories.name: Training & Enablement
ideas: Peer coaching and super-user support desks post-launch

categories.name: Technology & Process
ideas: Phased rollout to pilot group before full deployment
Data migration plan to preserve historical call records

categories.name: Measurement & Feedback
ideas: Baseline metrics captured before go-live for comparison
Dashboard visible to associates tracking their own KPIs

recommendation: Recommend AllHealthy execute a structured three-phase change management program: (1) Prepare — align leadership, identify change champions, establish communication channels, and baseline current metrics before go-live; (2) Launch — execute role-based training, activate the change agent network, and deploy with visible leadership support; (3) Sustain — measure adoption against defined KPIs (75% active users, improved call resolution time, higher customer and employee satisfaction), provide ongoing coaching, and tie continued use to performance management.

Prioritize contact center associates as the highest-impact stakeholder group given they are the primary users and their productivity and satisfaction are the main levers for customer experience improvement.
risks: Leadership misalignment at mid-management levels could undermine front-line adoption
Insufficient training depth leading to workarounds and continued use of legacy system
Change fatigue if communications are too frequent or poorly targeted
Failure to baseline current metrics making success measurement ambiguous
next_steps: Conduct stakeholder mapping workshop within first two weeks
Draft communication plan and identify change champions network
Define and agree on success metrics with AllHealthy leadership before any system deployment begins
Design role-based training curriculum and schedule pilot group for early testing
